name: Operator review and sign-off
summary: Track3D operations' quality control after processing: point-cloud verification, registration and sign-off in Antman, one reviewer at a time, the manual outcome tools in the TechOps view, and how a signed-off result reaches the customer.

roles.note: Review is done by Track3D staff in Antman, identified by email. Antman has no product roles of its own in the traced code, so grants for project roles are deny or unknown. Who may sign off is DEC-057; identity is DEC-059.

requirements.title: Non-image runs pass verification, registration and sign-off; image runs stop at processing complete
requirements.statement: When a non-image processing run succeeds it waits for point-cloud verification. Passing verification moves it to registration, or straight to sign-off when the run is set to register automatically. Registration complete leads to sign-off, which is approved or rejected. 360 image and phone image runs end at processing complete with no operator review. Antman refuses any other status change, and refuses all changes from a final state.

requirements.title: One reviewer at a time, and an abandoned review returns to the queue
requirements.statement: Each review step is claimed by one reviewer. A run can have only one active verification, registration or sign-off session, and only the claiming reviewer can send heartbeats or submit it. A session with no heartbeat for five minutes is marked abandoned and the run goes back to ready for that step. Status updates check the previous status, so two competing changes can't both win.

requirements.title: (Current behaviour) Sign-off publishes by writing the reality status directly
requirements.statement: Approving sign-off asks the platform to set the reality active; rejecting sets it inactive. This call writes only the status field. It skips the required-file check and the snapshot, zone coverage and turnaround updates that normal activation does (PROC-REQ-011). Antman records sign-off first and only logs a failed platform call, so signed off doesn't prove the customer can see the result. Antman's ops view also offers the full activation.

requirements.title: Successful 360 image automation updates the reality, and failures alert the review team
requirements.statement: When a 360 image capture is processed successfully, the system updates the reality status without manual steps. When automation fails and the reality is left in review, the review team is notified so they can act.
